words: how; what in ‘what is your name?’
My name is Sam. And you?
Excuse me, I do not understand that.
I would like a large tea.
Which country do you come from?
die Studenten; feminine: die Studentin / die Studentinnen
die Universitäten; short form: die Uni
I would like a loaf of bread.
I do not have any money with me.
The station is on the left.
The university is on the right.
Wir treffen uns um fünf Uhr.
We are meeting at five o'clock.
Ich stehe um sechs Uhr auf.
I get up at six o'clock.
Morgen um neun Uhr habe ich Zeit.
I am free tomorrow at nine o'clock.
die Uhren (clocks); time phrases use Uhr
Wir treffen uns um zehn Uhr.
We are meeting at ten o'clock.
ich stehe auf · du stehst auf
Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
I get up at seven o'clock.
I drink tea in the mornings.
die Zeiten (times); usually singular for available time
to suit; to work for someone
die Stockwerke; im ersten Stock = on the first floor
The stairs are on the right.
The door is on the left.
Der Kurs ist in diesem Gebäude.
The course is in this building.
Mein Deutschkurs beginnt um zehn Uhr.
My German class starts at ten o'clock.
Ich schreibe die Antwort ins Heft.
I write the answer in the exercise book.
We eat in the university canteen.
die Mittage; zu Mittag = for lunch
What are you doing around lunchtime today?
ich komme mit · du kommst mit
usually singular; Hunger haben = to be hungry
What are you doing at the weekend?
Am Sonntag besuche ich einen Freund.
On Sunday I am visiting a friend.
We are meeting in the park.
die Freunde; feminine: die Freundin / die Freundinnen
I am visiting friends on Sunday.
Ich arbeite zehn Stunden pro Woche.
I work ten hours per week.
Am Donnerstag habe ich einen Kurs.
I have a class on Thursday.
Ich kann ab zehn Uhr arbeiten.
I can work from ten o'clock.
ich fange an · du fängst an
After that I send the file.
I will send you the file.
Ich kann die Datei nicht öffnen.
die Erfahrungen; usually singular for work experience
I like working in a team.
I am looking for a job.
I am looking for a working-student job.
I am new to the team.

lessons.goal: Ask where your classroom is and check the floor or door before going there.
patterns: Say the room number after Raum. If you cannot find it, say: Ich finde den Raum nicht.
Use this to confirm the floor. Stockwerk means a floor; im ersten Stock is the common location phrase. In Germany, erster Stock is above the ground floor.
dialogue: Rechts. Dann ist es die erste Tür links.
On the right. Then it is the first door on the left.
The first door on the left?
practice: Ask for the room you need.
Der Kurs ist im ersten Stock.
The class is on the first floor.
Repeat one important direction to check it.
The first door on the left.
The first door on the left?
variations: You know the building but cannot find the room. Ask for help.
Your class is on the ground floor today. Check what you heard.
Heute ist der Kurs im Erdgeschoss.
Today the class is on the ground floor.
On the ground floor? Thank you!

lessons.goal: Tell a classmate you have a question and ask for an explanation or a demonstration.
patterns: Use du with a classmate. Mir means to me here; learn the question as a useful whole.
Use zeigen for a demonstration and erklären for an explanation.
dialogue: Ich habe eine Frage. Kannst du mir helfen?
I have a question. Can you help me?
I do not understand question two.
I will explain it to you.
Kannst du mir das im Heft zeigen?
Can you show me that in the exercise book?
practice: Tell your classmate you have a question.
Ask to see it in the exercise book.
The answer is in the exercise book.
variations: You need a short demonstration, not a long explanation. Ask for it.
Ja, bitte. Kannst du mir das zeigen?
Yes, please. Can you show me that?
Your classmate has explained it again. Tell them whether you understand now.
Yes, thank you. Now I understand.

lessons.goal: Invite someone to lunch, accept or decline kindly, and agree when to go.
patterns: Use this as a short invitation. In der Mensa means in the university canteen.
Kommst du mit? / Ich komme mit.
Are you coming along? / I am coming along.
Mitkommen separates: mit goes at the end. Nein, danke. Heute nicht. is a friendly short refusal.
dialogue: Ich gehe in die Mensa. Kommst du mit?
I am going to the canteen. Are you coming along?
Wir essen heute um ein Uhr.
We are eating at one o’clock today.
Ja. Das Essen schmeckt heute gut.
Yes. The food tastes good today.
practice: Invite a classmate to eat together.
Kommst du mit in die Mensa?
Are you coming along to the canteen?
Ask what time you are going.
variations: You cannot join today. Decline politely.
Nein, danke. Heute kann ich nicht.
No, thank you. I cannot today.
You have already started lunch. Give a simple opinion of the food.
Does it taste good to you?

lessons.goal: Describe a simple weekend plan and ask what your friend plans to do.
patterns: Put the verb next when the day comes first: Am Samstag besuche ich Freunde. Present tense can describe a plan when you give the day.
Use a real plan: einen Freund, eine Freundin, or Freunde. You can also say: Ich habe noch keinen Plan. (I have no plan yet.)
dialogue: What are you doing at the weekend?
Am Samstag besuche ich einen Freund.
On Saturday I am visiting a friend.
Da habe ich Zeit. Und du?
Then I am free. And you?
Ich gehe in den Park. Kommst du mit?
I am going to the park. Are you coming along?
practice: Give one real or clearly imagined Saturday plan.
What are you doing on Saturday?
Say whether you are free on Sunday.
Do you have time on Sunday?
Ja, am Sonntag habe ich Zeit.
Yes, I have time on Sunday.
Und du? Was machst du am Wochenende?
And you? What are you doing at the weekend?
variations: Suggest meeting in the park on Sunday.
Wo treffen wir uns am Sonntag?
Where shall we meet on Sunday?
You do not have a plan yet. Say so, then ask for your partner’s plan.
What are you doing at the weekend?
Ich habe noch keinen Plan. Und du?
I have no plan yet. And you?

lessons.goal: Give your real available days, weekly hours, and a possible starting time in short answers.
patterns: Use your actual days. For every Tuesday, say dienstags (on Tuesdays); am Dienstag means on Tuesday.
Ab gives the beginning; bis gives the end. These short answers are enough when the question is clear.
dialogue: Wie viele Stunden pro Woche können Sie arbeiten?
How many hours per week can you work?
An welchen Tagen sind Sie verfügbar?
On which days are you available?
Ab wann können Sie am Dienstag arbeiten?
From what time can you work on Tuesday?
practice: Give your own realistic number of weekly hours.
Wie viele Stunden pro Woche können Sie arbeiten?
How many hours per week can you work?
Name days that actually work for you.
An welchen Tagen haben Sie Zeit?
On which days do you have time?
Give your starting time for one day.
Ab wie viel Uhr können Sie arbeiten?
From what time can you work?
variations: One suggested day does not work. Say so and offer another.
Leider nicht. Am Dienstag habe ich Zeit.
Unfortunately not. I have time on Tuesday.
Give the time you need to finish.
Bis wie viel Uhr haben Sie Zeit?
Until what time do you have time?

lessons.goal: Ask a colleague what to do first, confirm a simple next step, and say when you have finished.
patterns: Zuerst means first. Ask this instead of guessing when there are several tasks.
Examples: Danach schicke ich die Datei. Ich bin fertig. Keep the verb directly after Danach.
dialogue: And what do I do after that?
Danach schickst du mir die Datei.
After that you send me the file.
practice: Danach schickst du mir die Datei.
After that you send me the file.
Danach schicke ich dir die Datei.
After that I will send you the file.
variations: You are ready but do not know when to begin. Ask.
You finished the first step and need the next one.
What do I do after that?

lessons.goal: Describe one simple problem at work and ask a colleague for help.
patterns: Ich habe ein Problem. / Ich brauche Hilfe.
I have a problem. / I need help.
Start with one short sentence, then add the problem. You do not need a long explanation.
Ich kann die Datei nicht öffnen.
After kann, the action word öffnen goes at the end. If the file is missing, use Die Datei fehlt.
dialogue: Ich kann die Datei nicht öffnen.
Ich schicke sie dir noch einmal.
I will send it to you again.
practice: Tell your colleague you need help.
Say that the file will not open.
Ich kann die Datei nicht öffnen.
Say that the problem is fixed and thank them.
Yes, now it works. Thank you!
variations: The file is missing rather than broken. Explain the difference.
Ask for the file to be sent again.
Kannst du die Datei bitte noch einmal schicken?
Can you send the file again, please?

lessons.goal: Give a short work introduction using your name, studies or current activity, and one true interest or strength.
warmup: I like working in a team.
patterns: Two short sentences are enough to start. Change the model to your real name and current situation.
Ich arbeite gern … / Ich habe Erfahrung mit …
I like working … / I have experience with …
Choose something true. You can also say Ich habe noch keine Erfahrung. (I do not have experience yet.) Then say what you want to learn.
dialogue: Guten Tag! Stellen Sie sich kurz vor.
Ich heiße Sam. Ich studiere Informatik.
My name is Sam. I study computer science.
I am looking for a working-student job.
I like working in a team.
practice: Introduce yourself in two short sentences.
Stellen Sie sich bitte kurz vor.
Ich heiße Sam. Ich studiere Informatik.
My name is Sam. I study computer science.
Name one real interest or strength.
I like working in a team.
Ask one simple question about the work.
What would my first task be?
variations: You are meeting a team for the first time. Introduce yourself as a new person.
Ich heiße Sam. Ich bin neu im Team.
My name is Sam. I am new to the team.
Someone asks about experience. Give one truthful example, or say you are just starting.
Not yet. I would like to learn.

lessons.goal: Ask for a simple food item, add another item if needed, and say when that is everything.
patterns: Practise complete items: ein Brot, einen Apfel, zwei Äpfel, Milch. Milk usually needs no article when asking for some.
Use Noch … to add something. Nein, danke. answers Noch etwas? (Anything else?).
dialogue: Ein Brot, bitte. Ist es frisch?
A loaf of bread, please. Is it fresh?
practice: Ask for a loaf of bread or an apple.
Add an item to your order.
Say that you do not need anything else.
variations: This time you only need milk. Ask for it.
What would you like to buy?
I would like some milk, please.
Ask whether the bread is fresh before ordering.
Would you like a loaf of bread?

lessons.goal: Ask how much an item costs, choose cash or card, and check a price you did not catch.
patterns: Pointing to the item is enough. Das stands for the thing you want to buy.
Mit Karte means by card. Bar means in cash. You can answer simply: Mit Karte, bitte.
dialogue: How much does the bread cost?
practice: Ask for the price of an item.
You would like this loaf of bread.
variations: The shop accepts cash only. Say that you will pay cash.
You heard two euros. Confirm rather than guess.

lessons.goal: Ask where a place is, recognise left/right/straight ahead, and confirm one direction.
patterns: Examples: der Bahnhof, die Universität. Start with Entschuldigung to get someone’s attention politely.
Repeat one important direction to check it. You can also ask: Ist das nah? (Is that close?).
dialogue: Excuse me, where is the train station?
Gehen Sie geradeaus und dann links.
Go straight ahead and then left.
Ja. Der Bahnhof ist ganz nah.
Yes. The station is very close.
practice: Ask where the train station is.
You are looking for the train station.
Excuse me, where is the train station?
Gehen Sie geradeaus und dann rechts.
Go straight ahead and then right.
Ask whether the place is close.
Der Bahnhof ist in dieser Straße.
The station is in this street.
variations: Ask for the university instead of the station.
You are unsure whether you should turn left. Check it.
The station is on the left.

lessons.goal: Say simple numbers and whole-hour times, and distinguish the current time from an appointment time.
patterns: Start with whole hours. Ein Uhr means one o’clock: use ein, not eins, immediately before Uhr.
Use um for the time of an activity. We begin with 1–5 and 10; the next lessons add 6–9. German also uses the 24-hour clock.
dialogue: Treffen wir uns um vier Uhr?
Shall we meet at four o’clock?
practice: Imagine the clock shows ten. Say the time.
Um wie viel Uhr treffen wir uns?
At what time shall we meet?
Confirm that you heard four, not five.
Wir treffen uns um vier Uhr.
We will meet at four o’clock.
variations: Now the clock shows one. Say the time.
A friend suggests two o’clock. Agree and repeat the time.

lessons.goal: Say when you get up and eat, then give one simple detail about your routine.
warmup: Ich stehe um sechs Uhr auf.
I get up at six o’clock.
patterns: Aufstehen separates: stehe goes after ich, and auf goes at the end. Use your real time.
Change the time to fit your routine. Morgens means in the mornings; morgen without s means tomorrow.
dialogue: Ich stehe um sechs Uhr auf.
I get up at six o’clock.
When do you eat in the morning?
practice: Ich stehe um sechs Uhr auf.
I get up at six o’clock.
Say when you eat in the morning.
When do you eat in the morning?
variations: Give your routine for a different day, such as a day with no classes.
When do you get up then?
Ich stehe um acht Uhr auf.
I get up at eight o’clock.
Ask a friend about their morning.

lessons.goal: Ask whether a friend has time, choose a day and time, and confirm the plan.
patterns: Use heute (today), morgen (tomorrow), or am Montag (on Monday).
Uns belongs with treffen when saying we meet each other. Repeat the day and time at the end.
practice: Ask a friend whether they have time tomorrow.
You would like to meet me.
variations: A friend is free today. Suggest a time that works for you.
Treffen wir uns um neun Uhr?
Shall we meet at nine o’clock?

lessons.goal: Say when a time does not work, suggest another time, and confirm the change.
patterns: This is a polite, useful short sentence. Add another possibility rather than a long explanation.
Examples: Passt Freitag? Freitag passt gut. You can propose a whole day or a time.
dialogue: Passt der Termin morgen um neun Uhr?
Does the appointment tomorrow at nine work?
Leider nicht. Geht es auch später?
Unfortunately not. Would later work too?
practice: Say that the proposed time does not work.
Accept the new time and repeat it.
variations: Suggest another day instead of another time.
A friend asks to change the time. Accept if it works for you.
Geht es morgen um fünf Uhr?
Would tomorrow at five o’clock work?
Ja, morgen um fünf Uhr passt gut.
Yes, tomorrow at five o’clock works well.

lessons.goal: Tell someone that you are learning German and can speak only a little. Ask for a manageable conversation.
patterns: Ich lerne describes what you are learning. You do not need to claim you speak well.
Ein bisschen is a useful way to set expectations. Nein, noch nicht. means No, not yet.
dialogue: Do you already speak a lot of German?
practice: Say that you are learning German.
Say how much German you speak honestly.
Say that you do not understand this yet.
variations: A new neighbour starts speaking to you. Explain that you are learning.
A little. I am learning German.
A classmate offers to practise slowly with you. Accept and thank them.

lessons.goal: Give your surname, spell it slowly, and ask someone to spell theirs.
patterns: Use your own name. German names are examples, not names you need to adopt.
Say one letter at a time. Try the audio for S – A – M, then practise your own letters. Ä, Ö, Ü and ß are additional German letters; ß is called Eszett.
practice: Ask someone to spell an unfamiliar name.
variations: You are registering for a course. Repeat and spell your surname.
How do you write your surname?
Meyer. M – E – Y – E – R.
Meyer. M – E – Y – E – R.
The receptionist reads back the wrong spelling. Correct it gently.

lessons.goal: Say where you live and where you come from, then ask the question back.
patterns: Use in with a city: in Berlin, in Köln. Put your own city in the gap.
Use your real place of origin. Examples: aus Indien, aus Spanien. Some countries use an article: aus der Türkei, aus den USA.
dialogue: Ich wohne in Köln. Und du?
I live in Cologne. And you?
Ich wohne auch hier. Woher kommst du?
I live here too. Where do you come from?
practice: Say the city or town you live in.
Give your own place of origin.
Ask your partner where they live.
variations: You meet a neighbour. Say that you live here too.
At a language class, give both your city and your place of origin.
Ich wohne in Köln. Ich komme aus Indien.
I live in Cologne. I come from India.

lessons.goal: Say which languages you speak and ask for simple German when you need it.
patterns: Ich spreche … und ein bisschen Deutsch.
I speak … and a little German.
Language names usually have no article here. Use languages you actually speak.
Use this with a classmate. You can also ask for English: Auf Englisch, bitte.
dialogue: Ich spreche Englisch und ein bisschen Deutsch.
I speak English and a little German.
Gut! Können wir einfaches Deutsch sprechen?
Good! Can we speak simple German?
practice: Noch nicht. Ich spreche ein bisschen Deutsch.
Not yet. I speak a little German.
variations: A classmate also speaks one of your languages. Say that you do too.
You need a short English explanation before trying again in German.

lessons.goal: Explain in one or two sentences what you study or do. Use your real situation.
patterns: Choose your real subject. Informatik, Biologie, and Wirtschaft are examples.
Ich bin Student. / Ich bin Studentin.
Choose the form that fits you. If you are not a student, use Ich arbeite … or describe what you currently do.
dialogue: Ich bin Student. Ich studiere Informatik.
I am a student. I study computer science.
An der Universität hier in Köln.
At the university here in Cologne.
Not yet. I am looking for work.
practice: Say what you study, or what you currently do.
Name your own university or place of work.
Where do you study or work?
Ask your classmate about their studies.
variations: Introduce yourself with your name and one fact about your studies or work.
Ich heiße Sam. Ich studiere Informatik.
My name is Sam. I study computer science.
A classmate asks whether you also have a job. Answer truthfully.

lessons.goal: Say something you enjoy, something you prefer, and ask about the other person’s interests.
patterns: Examples: Ich lese gern. Ich koche gern. For a dislike, add nicht before gern: Ich koche nicht gern.
Lieber compares choices: Ich lese lieber. means I would rather read.
dialogue: Ich koche gern und mache Sport.
I like cooking and doing sport.
Ich spiele Fußball. Spielst du auch?
I play football. Do you play too?
No. I prefer listening to music.
practice: Name one thing you genuinely enjoy.
Liest du lieber oder kochst du lieber?
Do you prefer reading or cooking?
variations: A classmate suggests sport. Say whether you like it.
You prefer a quiet activity. Explain your preference simply.
Would you like to play football?
No, thank you. I would rather read.

lessons.goal: Say hello, give your name, and ask the other person's name. One short sentence is enough.
patterns: After ich, use heiße. Put your own name in the gap.
Use du with a classmate. Und du? is a short way to ask the question back.
practice: Now ask a new classmate their name.
variations: A second classmate joins you. Greet them and say your name.
Hallo! Ich heiße Kim. Wie heißt du?
Hello! My name is Kim. What is your name?
Hello, Kim! My name is Sam.
You arrive first at a language class. Introduce yourself and ask a name.
Hallo! Ich heiße Sam. Wie heißt du?
Hello! My name is Sam. What is your name?

lessons.goal: Keep a conversation going when you do not understand: ask for repetition and slower speech.
patterns: Learn this as a whole useful sentence. Sie is polite, for someone you do not know.
The shorter Bitte langsam. also communicates the request.
dialogue: Entschuldigung. Können Sie das bitte wiederholen?
Excuse me. Can you repeat that, please?
practice: Ask politely to hear the sentence again.
variations: At a shop, you miss the price. Ask to hear it again.
Someone explains the way too fast. Ask them to slow down.
Gehen Sie links und dann rechts.

lessons.goal: Order one drink, choose its size, and finish politely.
patterns: Use einen Kaffee / einen Tee, but ein Wasser. Practise the drink together with its little word.
A short answer is natural when someone asks about the size.
dialogue: I would like a coffee, please.
practice: Order a coffee, tea, or water.
What would you like to drink?
I would like a tea, please.
variations: This time, order water instead of coffee.
Order for yourself and a friend: one coffee and one tea.
What would you like to drink?
Einen Kaffee und einen Tee, bitte.
A coffee and a tea, please.
